paper_title: A Telescope Search for Decaying Relic Axions
suggested_experiment_name: VIMOS/VLT Integral Field Unit Spectroscopy of Abell 2667 and 2390
coupling_convention: ξ (dimensionless two-photon coupling parameter), as plotted on y-axis. Note: ξ relates to g_agamma via ξ = g_agamma * m_a / (2π), where m_a is axion mass in eV and g_agamma is in GeV^-1. The plotted values are the dimensionless coupling ξ directly from the exclusion plot.
notes: New upper limits on axion two-photon coupling from optical line emission search in galaxy clusters Abell 2667 and 2390 using VIMOS integral field unit at VLT. Mass range 4.5–7.7 eV set by usable wavelength range (4000–6800 Å). Limits improve on previous work by factor of 2.1–7.1. Data points extracted from Table I (central line intensity and ξ at candidate axion masses). The coupling parameter ξ is defined in Eq. (3) as ξ ≡ (4/3)(E/N − 1.92 ± 0.08), where E and N depend on axion model; this parameterization allows model-independent limits. Assumes standard thermal freeze-out axion abundance (Eq. 1). Analysis uses strong-lensing mass models from HST data to weight spatial regions and optimize signal-to-noise. No axion decay signal detected; limits rule out canonical KSVZ and DFSZ models in this mass window but theoretical uncertainties allow wider range of ξ values. Cross-correlation analysis (Table II) yields slightly less stringent limits (~1.5× weaker). The x-axis spans 4.5–7.7 eV (linear scale), y-axis spans 1e-09 to 1e-07 (log scale). The solid curve represents the observational limit from this work; dashed curves show theoretical predictions (KSVZ and DFSZ models). The shaded region above the solid curve is excluded. Narrow features labeled 'Sky Lines' near 5.7 eV and 6.3 eV indicate wavelengths where sky subtraction is unreliable. The coupling ξ is dimensionless and represents the two-photon decay amplitude. Values extracted from the lower boundary of the exclusion region by visual inspection of the plotted curve. The paper reports these limits are at least 3× more stringent than previous constraints in this mass window. Conversion to canonical g_agamma [GeV^-1] would require the relation g_agamma = 2π·ξ/m_a, but per the plotted-values contract, emitted values are ξ as directly plotted. | Calibration: No calibration needed
